idiom_name: net.Listener accept loop + goroutine per connection; http.Server.Serve
implementation_notes: The stdlib embodies the split: net.Listen is the acceptor role, net.Dial/net.DialContext the connector, and net/http.Server.Serve(l, handler) runs the accept loop, spawns the per-connection goroutine and dispatches to the Handler — the roles disappear into the runtime. Custom protocols use the explicit loop ``for { c, err := ln.Accept(); go handle(c) }``. Graceful drain is achieved by calling srv.Shutdown(ctx), which stops Accept() and waits for in-flight handlers; set ReadHeaderTimeout to avoid slow-client resource exhaustion. SetKeepAlive only configures TCP keep-alive; to share a port with independent listeners, use net.ListenConfig.Control to set SO_REUSEPORT before bind on platforms that support it.
pitfalls: Do not spin on accept errors and do not exit the loop for recoverable resource-exhaustion errors — back off instead.
Unbounded ``go handle(conn)`` is a resource-exhaustion vector; bound it with a worker pool or semaphore.
Closing the listener stops Accept but not in-flight connections; drain them with context timeouts.
ReadHeaderTimeout limits the time to read request headers; without it a slow client can hold a goroutine indefinitely.
net/http.Server.Shutdown does not close idle connections; use Server.Close for immediate shutdown.
